How to use this calculator

  1. Enter area to tile, tile length, tile width and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How tile is calculated

Estimate tile count from floor area and individual tile dimensions, with an adjustable cutting and breakage allowance. The calculation rounds up to whole tiles and excludes grout spacing, pattern cuts, spare stock, and carton pack sizes unless you account for them in the allowance. A 100 ft² floor covered by 1 ft² tiles with 10% extra requires 110 tiles. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Yes, a suitable reserve helps cover cuts, breakage, and future repairs. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

tile count = ceiling(area ÷ tile area × (1 + allowance))
A worked example

A 100 ft² floor covered by 1 ft² tiles with 10% extra requires 110 tiles.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Should I order extra tiles?

Yes, a suitable reserve helps cover cuts, breakage, and future repairs.

Does it calculate cartons?

No. Divide the rounded tile count by the package yield and round up separately.
